Subject: Redwood benchmarks — latency & throughput A/B test (post-call recap)

Thanks again for the time earlier today — great convo and appreciate you sharing the benchmark harness. Per our call, attached are the raw results and a short PDF summary highlighting the A/B comparisons we ran between Redwood and the hyperscaler endpoints you asked about. High-level recap here so we have a single thread for next steps.

Summary of the runs (model variant: Llama-2-70B-Chat, 4-bit quantized):
- Test config: 60s bursts, payload size ~128 tokens per request, steady concurrency windows at 10/50/100 RPS; sessions use prefix caching where applicable.
- Redwood (dedicated inference config, nv4x2 equivalent): p50 = 18 ms/token, p95 = 120 ms/token, p99 = 220 ms/token; sustained throughput ~1,800 tokens/sec at 100 RPS (across pool), average GPU util 62%.
- AWS Bedrock (comparable model offering): p50 = 35 ms/token, p95 = 330 ms/token, p99 = 710 ms/token; sustained throughput reported ~900 tokens/sec in our harness.
- Azure OpenAI (gpt-style managed endpoint): p50 = 30 ms/token, p95 = 290 ms/token, p99 = 640 ms/token; throughput ~1,000 tokens/sec.

Key observations:
- Redwood shows consistently lower p95/p99 on these bursty workloads due to continuous batching + KV cache behavior. The difference is most pronounced at 50–100 RPS.
- Throughput delta scales with batching aggressiveness; Redwood's runtime picks kernel paths that reduce per-token overhead for this model family.
- Quality (log-perplexity / top-k sampling traces) looked comparable in our A/B pass — we didn't see obvious generation regressions in the short runs but we should run longer prompt suites.

Attachments included: globex_abtest_results_20260625.csv (raw logs), redwood-vs-hyperscalers-20260625.pdf (summary + charts).

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Redwood to run a longer 30-minute sustained test at 100 RPS with the same prompt set to capture steady-state behavior and KV cache warmup effects. We will also capture GPU-level metrics (util, mem, SM %, power) and KV cache hit rates. (Owner: Connor)
2) Add a quality/regression sweep with your in-house prompt set (10k tokens total) to verify output parity. If you share the set, we can run in a redacted mode on a dedicated pool. (Owner: Marissa + Laura)
3) Schedule a follow-up demo to walk through the telemetry and tuning knobs (batching, quantization profile, routing fallback). Proposed window: Tue 30 Jun 09:00 PT — let me know if that works.

If helpful, we can also spin up a short canary in us-west-2 with your sample traffic (we'd need a small service account + short-lived API key).

Thanks — attaching results now.
—
Marissa Cole
